summary: Daughter of Bull Smith who married William Lawrence of Flushing, Governor Philip Carteret of New Jersey and Colonel Richard Townley; John's 9th-great-grand-aunt.
bio:
Elizabeth Smith, a daughter of Bull Smith of Smithtown, was John's 9th-great-grand-aunt and married three times. Her first husband, William Lawrence of Flushing, had come to America on the Planter in 1635 with his stepfather John Tuttell; at his death his estate was valued at 2,021 pounds, with his sword, plate and personal effects appraised separately at a high figure. Through him she became the ancestress of the Flushing Lawrence cousins.

In 1681 she married Philip Carteret, Governor of New Jersey, under a prenuptial agreement that kept Tew's Neck for her Lawrence sons; she had no children by Carteret. Her third husband, Colonel Richard Townley, had come over in 1683 with Lord Howard of Effingham, the Governor of Virginia. Carteret and Townley are connected to the family by marriage only.
sources: Lawrence, Historical Genealogy of the Lawrence Family (1858), https://archive.org/details/historicalgeneal00lawr
